capture: per-test coverage carry, @TestSetup coverage and async work, trigger listing in sync and async runs (cov-r2)
captured: 2026-11-17 (UTC)
orgs: fresh 1-day Developer scratch orgs on two campaign Dev Hubs, one main org per API plus fresh orgs for the f7 steps; every org deleted and verified gone
sf: @salesforce/cli 2.157.8
class apis: 62.0 and 67.0 (every .cls-meta.xml and .trigger-meta.xml)
fixtures: fixtures/main (main org), fixtures/f7 (f7 orgs)
steps (main org, repeats r1 and r2 in the same org):
  mix-full           sf apex run test --class-names CarryMixTest --synchronous --code-coverage
  mix-gamma          --tests CarryMixTest.Gamma --synchronous
  mix-full-async     --class-names CarryMixTest (asynchronous)
  setup              --class-names CarrySetupTest --synchronous
  x12-par-on         --class-names CarryX1Test,CarryX2Test, parallel Apex testing enabled
  x12-par-off        the same with parallel Apex testing disabled (ApexSettings)
  Setup*Test         --class-names <class> --synchronous; each test method reports what it sees through its failure message (FACTS ...)
  setup-all-async    every Setup*Test class in one asynchronous run
steps (f7, fresh org each): f7a = aLeft,bRight async then sync; f7b = aLeft sync then aLeft,bRight async
  The 62.0 f7a r2 async run returned no results within the wait and is omitted. The 67.0 f7b r2 org was not created (hub limit); its rows are absent.
columns: api, repeat, step, kind, test_class, method, component, covered, detail
  test  one test method of the step's run: detail = Outcome|Message
  run   sf run summary: testRunCoverage and the coverage list (read from stored aggregates)
  per   Tooling ApexCodeCoverage row of a test class the step ran, queried right after the step; covered = covered lines
notes:
  Per-test and test rows are identical between repeats and between the two APIs. Run summaries differ between repeats
  because they read the org's stored aggregates.
  Carry order is by code point (Alpha, Gamma, Zeta, apple, beta, delta). Carry stays inside one test class.
  @TestSetup coverage is in the first test row of the class in that order only.
  A synchronous run lists every trigger in every per-test row and in its summary; an asynchronous run lists only what tests reached.
  A setup whose async job throws, or chains another Queueable, fails every method and the class has no per-test rows.
